ui.updates.service.release_publishing.me: A new server release ({version}) is still publishing, so no update was offered yet. Check again in a few minutes.
ui.updates.service.version_unknown.messa: The installed server version could not be determined, so no update was offered. Restart the app to try again.
ui.updates.service.attempt_running.messa: A server update this app started at a time that could not be read is still running (process group {group}), so a second one will not be started beside it. If that update is no longer responding, the update service log says what it was doing.

A server update this app started moments ago is still running (process group {group}), so a second one will not be started beside it. If that update is no longer responding, the update service log says what it was doing.

A server update this app started {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} ago is still running (process group {group}), so a second one will not be started beside it. If that update is no longer responding, the update service log says what it was doing.
ui.updates.service.already_running.messa: A server update is already running. Let it finish before starting another.
ui.updates.service.install_not_found.mes: The global install could not be found on this machine, so the update did not run. See the update service log.
ui.updates.service.no_restart.message: The server was updated but the backend did not restart. Restart Local Operator to run the new version.
ui.updates.service.no_restart_properly.m: The server was updated but the backend did not restart properly. Restart Local Operator to run the new version.
ui.updates.service.start_mode_unknown.me: The app could not tell how this server was started, so it did not update it. See the update service log.
ui.updates.service.no_server_reference.m: The app has no server to update right now. Restart Local Operator and try again.
ui.updates.service.release_unreadable.me: The app could not read which release to install, so it left its server environment alone. Check the connection and try again.
ui.updates.service.disk_space.message: The server update needs about {needed, number, ::group-off} MB of free space on this disk, and {free, number, ::group-off} MB is free, so the app left the environment serving this app alone. Free some space and try again.
ui.updates.service.not_installed.message: The server update did not install, so the environment serving this app was left as it was.
ui.updates.service.install_in_flight.mes: Version {version} can't finish installing while Local Operator is open — keeping it open cancels the install. Quit and leave it closed until the app opens again by itself.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.not_ru: The server update did not finish: the installer could not be run to a verdict.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.exited: The server update did not install: `{command}` exited {code}.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.rebuil: The rebuild finished but did not change this install: its `.lop-source` still names the same revision.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.not_ef: The server update to {target} did not take effect: the install still reports {installed}.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.stoppe: The updater was stopped; something it started may still be replacing the install.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.pointe: The installer's own output is below.
The installer's own output is in the update service log.
ui.updates.service.server_failure.run_yo: You can also run `{command}` yourself in a terminal.
ui.updates.service.fleet.closing: Nothing was installed and the server keeps running the build it loaded; the app will offer this update again.
ui.updates.service.fleet.unknown.credent: The server refused this app's credentials, so the app could not read which sessions are running on this machine.
ui.updates.service.fleet.unknown.unreada: The app could not read which sessions are running on this machine, so it did not update the server.
ui.updates.service.fleet.unknown.body: Reading an unreadable fleet as idle could cut off a turn that is in flight, so the app waited {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} and then stopped. {closing}
ui.updates.service.fleet.busy.none_named: The app could not name the sessions that were still working.
ui.updates.service.fleet.busy.lead: {count, plural, one {# session is} other {# sessions are}} still running a turn on this machine: {names}{extra, plural, =0 {} other { and # more}}.
ui.updates.service.fleet.busy.body: The app waited {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} for them to finish and then stopped rather than cut a turn short. {closing}
ui.updates.service.global.source_build.r: The server is running from a source checkout on this machine rather than an installed copy, so update it with lop-update after your change is merged.
ui.updates.service.global.pipx.remedy: The server is a pipx install, so update it from your terminal
ui.updates.service.global.pip.remedy: The server is a pip install, so update it from your terminal
ui.updates.service.global.unknown.remedy: The app could not tell how this server was installed, so update it with the tool you installed it with - uv, pipx or pip
ui.updates.service.global.source_rebuild: Rebuilds this checkout with `lop-update`. The app waits for the turns running on this machine to finish first, and the rebuild then reinstalls this install in place - so a turn started while it runs can still be interrupted - and it can take up to half an hour. This install keeps reporting the checkout's version, not the release the app offered.
ui.updates.service.global.legacy_install: This install predates the non-disruptive installer, so update it once from your terminal; that updater rewrites the shared environment in place, which can interrupt sessions mid-turn. The app manages updates after that.
